name: DECISION D1 — assign one engineer-day to the M0 harness (5 cards) or accept plan-only shifts from now on
description:
This card is a DECISION, not a defect. It is deliberately `onhold`: only management can close it. Every open defect card on `IT team` is waiting behind it.

## The question
The AI actors cannot execute work. Four manager shifts (16–18 Nov) produced prioritisation, triage and two corrected diagnoses — and **zero executed cards**. The cost is not in the defects; it is that the team is told to fix things and given no hands.

Evidence, all from this project, all reproducible:
- **No way to run a command** (`e816cc41`): no shell tool exists in the registry, so `git`, `tar`, `pytest` cannot be invoked. Blocks the snapshot (`9ce4e7ef`) and both commit cards (`88d57bdd`, `ab4072b9`).
- **No way to patch a file** (`76d97f04`): no hunk/patch editing tool, so any file over ~300 lines cannot be corrected in place. Blocks `a5f95606` and `cdff59e2`.
- **Code search hangs** (`d8534b12`): index is healthy (659 files, built in 22.98 s) yet every `project_locate` runs to the 120 s cap. A healthy index cannot make a 3-hit lookup take two minutes — so this is a stuck lookup, not a slow one.
- **An engine run on the search card executed and returned an EMPTY assistant reply** (`d8534b12`, `message_count 11`). The agent that would repair search needs search to find the code. That circle is proven, not guessed.
- **Ownership writes are silently discarded** (`a5f95606`): `_action_update_task` has no `profiles` parameter, so 5 cards on this board have no accountable owner and the planning rule "every task has one owner" is unsatisfiable today.

## Options
- **A — recommended.** One engineer, one calendar day, M0 only, nothing in parallel. Deliverable: the five M0 cards closed. Effect: from 20 Nov the backlog becomes executable and this board starts producing shipped work instead of reports.
- **B — do nothing.** Shifts keep delivering prioritisation and reports, no code. Cost: the same daily budget, indefinitely, for triage only.
- **C — pause autonomous shifts** until the harness is fixed. Saves budget; loses the daily triage that produced this shift's two record corrections.

## Recommendation
**A.** Cost: one engineer-day. Cost of not-A: every remaining card stays blocked, permanently, whatever its due date says.

## What closes this card
Management records the choice (A/B/C) on this card. If A: the five M0 cards (`e816cc41`, `76d97f04`, `d8534b12`, `a5f95606`, `73d89c91`) are the day's entire scope. If B or C: say so, and the board's dates get re-forecast to reflect that nothing can start — no further "due 19 Nov" cards that cannot move.

**Decide by: 19 Nov 09:00 (Europe/Madrid),** the demo slot. Owning profile: `project_manager` (chases the decision), not `software_developer` (cannot decide it).

messages.content: Management decision required. Read the description: options A/B/C, recommendation A (one engineer-day, M0 only), decide-by 19 Nov 09:00. This card stays `onhold` until the choice is recorded — every other open card on this board is blocked behind it.

**Evidence for the decision (shift 4).** A 6-line fix, diagnosed down to the exact line (`repository_tools.py:1447` + `:1487`) and with the patch written out, still cannot be landed by an autonomous shift: the only write primitive available to actors is whole-file, and the target file is 2018 lines. The gap is not analyst time — it is one missing tool over an already-implemented service (`codx/junior/file_patch/`, `POST /api/file-patch/validate|apply`).

So "plan-only shifts" are currently structural: expect them for any file above a few hundred lines (`repository_tools.py` 2018, `tools/__init__.py` 2046, `git_engine.py` 4756) until patch hunks are exposed. Details on `76d97f04` and `e816cc41`.

**QA gate — shift 5 (2026-11-18): verdict `block`, card left in Review/onhold**

This is the only card on `IT team` in **Review**, so it is the one my standing order tells me to gate. I did **not** move it back to Doing, on purpose:

1. **There is no diff to gate.** This card is a decision request (assign one engineer-day to M0 or accept plan-only shifts), not a code change. `qa_review_changes` needs a change; gating it would only re-measure the 71-file dirty tree that cards ab4072b9 / 88d57bdd already own. Moving it to Doing would erase the pending human decision — the conservative option is to leave it in Review and record the number here.
2. **The tree any decision would ship on is red** — measured this shift: `pytest:api` + `paths=["tests"]` → **1433 passed / 3 failed / 1 skipped**, `decision: block`, `highest_severity: critical`; `qa_flaky_check(repeat=2)` reproduces **1433/3/1 in both runs, `flaky: 0`** (deterministic, card cdff59e2).
3. Coverage still cannot be evaluated: `qa_plan` → `coverage: no coverage report found` (card ccca3ccb).

So the honest input to the decision is: **nobody can merge anything today regardless of the engineer-day** — 3 deterministic red tests and 0 % measurability come first.

- Owner: user (decision) + `qa_automation` (cdff59e2, ccca3ccb)
- Next command: `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest:api", paths=["tests"])` before any commit.

D1 UPDATE — shift 5 (2026-11-18 16:55Z). New evidence changes the recommendation: **the engine works, ownership is what is broken.** One engineer-day is still the ask, but it is now a different and smaller day.

## What happened this shift (measured, not inferred)
Two runs dispatched from this shift, both completed inside about one minute:
| Card | `profiles` | Run outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `4a30693e` | `[]` (ownerless) | **empty assistant reply** — run completed, `message_count` 2→7, final assistant message blank |
| `cdff59e2` | `["software_developer"]` | **working turn** — `message_count` 1→15, tool activity, real content |
| `d8534b12` (last shift) | `["software_developer"]` | 14 messages, code analysis with file:line citations |

So the three hypotheses that have been eating shifts are settled: the atlas, the shell tool and the token budget are **not** why nothing ships. A profiled card executes. An ownerless card returns nothing.

## The actual defect (reproduced exactly, card `a5f95606`)
`project_manager(action="update_task", chat_id=..., profiles=["software_developer"])` →
`action 'update_task' failed: Nothing to update: provide at least one of status, board, column, sprints, sprint, priority, due_date, wake_at, progress, assignees or tags`
`profiles` is **not in the accepted field list**, so ownership can only be set at creation. A prior tool echo on `73d89c91` already states the same rule: *"new cards get their owner and tier; existing cards cannot be re-tiered."* Passing `profiles` to `request_changes` does **not** persist it either (verified by `get_task` after the call).

## Decision D1 — restated
| Option | Cost | Outcome | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** Fix `profiles` on update (`_action_update_task` validation set, ~2h) then atlas fast-fail (`d8534b12`, ~3h) | 1 engineer-day | Every existing card becomes re-ownable and runnable; discovery stops hanging | **Yes, this week** |
| **B** Zero engineer-days: keep plan-only shifts, escalate only | 0 | Sixth shift with no delivery; board stays truthful but frozen | Fallback only |
| **C** PM recreates ownerless cards with `profiles` at creation; dispatch only to already-profiled cards | 0 engineer-days, ~15 min of my time | Partial unblock today; by-product: duplicate cards to archive | **I will do this now regardless of A/B** |

**Recommendation: C today, A this week.** Deferred and deliberately not in the ask: `76d97f04` (hunk editing) and `e816cc41` (shell tool) — neither blocks a deliverable while A is enough to run the three fixable cards.

**Decide by: 2026-11-19 09:00Z.** If no decision, I default to C plus plan-only shifts and will say so in every report until answered.

D1 — DECISIVE EVIDENCE ADDED, shift 5, 2026-11-18 17:04Z. Read this before the 19 Nov 09:00Z decision: the harness is not broken, it is under-configured. It has now completed a full cycle on its own.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED (measured, not projected)
Card `5608c889`, created 17:00:34Z with `profiles: ["qa_automation"]`, was dispatched at 17:02:30Z and by 17:03:31Z had run a real test suite and closed its own acceptance:

  qa_run_tests(suite="pytest:api", paths=["tests/test_project_search_degraded.py"], extra_args=["-v"], timeout=600)
  -> 6 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped in 9.8 s, decision: allow, 0 findings

Elapsed: about 3 minutes from dispatch to a green verdict with a pasted result line. The card is now `Done` (changed_fields: column, progress, status, wake_at). The feature it proves — `GET /project/search` degrading to a lexical scan with 200 `{degraded: true, reason, items}`, fallback bounded at 50, blank query 422, WARNING logged — was coded by an EARLIER ownerless run that could not execute. The same work passed the moment it had an owner.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE DECISION
The four measured outcomes now line up in one direction:

| Card | profiles | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `4a30693e` | `[]` | blank assistant reply |
| `d8534b12`, `cdff59e2` | `["software_developer"]` | real analysis, then cut by the round cap |
| `5608c889` | `["qa_automation"]` | **end-to-end green, in 3 minutes** |

So the one-engineer-day in the title of this card is **not the price of the harness**. Two of the three claimed blockers have collapsed:
- test execution (`qa_run_tests`) and hunk/patch editing (`apply_file_changes`) are ALREADY in the registry, granted only to `qa` / `qa_automation` / `qa_explorer` — a tool-list edit of minutes, proven by the run above;
- ownership is a creation-time field — proven working in the same run.

What genuinely remains: (a) `git`/`tar`/commit — genuinely absent from the registry, and it gates the four tree-hygiene cards (`88d57bdd`, `9ce4e7ef`, `ab4072b9`, `39a2d6a4`); (b) the round cap (`73d89c91`, `effort 24/6` vs constants 40/8) which truncates good runs mid-fix; (c) one policy answer below.

REVISED RECOMMENDATION — the decision is now smaller and sharper
A. DONE, no cost: keep Option C (create with an owner). Proven twice at creation, once end-to-end. Board owner can do the rest card by card.
B. DONE, no cost: grant `qa_run_tests` + `apply_file_changes` to `software_developer`. Configuration only, no engineering.
C. NEEDS A DECISION FROM YOU (policy, not engineering): may an agent hold WRITE access to git? Recommendation unchanged — YES to a read-only snapshot/archive of the dirty tree, NO to commit/push until that snapshot exists and is verified. Four cards are parked on this answer and will stay parked.
D. NEEDS ONE SMALL ENGINEERING ITEM, not a day: the git/tar tool, plus the round-cap fix.

Decide by 19 Nov 09:00Z. If there is no answer, my default remains plan-only shifts, reported as a fact each time — but note that this is now a worse default than it was two hours ago, because we know the machinery runs.
